opportunities.goal: Verify h > 1891871140656049/1929687500000000 for every finite exact residue-class partition with at least two points per class.
opportunities.sector: Computer-assisted mathematics and reusable proof certificates
opportunities.successMetric: Two independently derived exact certificate implementations agree; all 78 short-class patches, the infinite-length tail and every finite n pass; the known invalid grid witness is refused. No external peer review or production qualification is asserted.
opportunities.thesis: An exact rational polynomial certificate replaces unbounded enumeration with a universal lower bound, independently recomputed in two implementations. This is a mathematical research result; priority, external review, commercial demand and model superiority are separate questions.
opportunities.title: A universal heft barrier for finite residue partitions

sources.excerpt: The author defines distinct-modulus residue classes that partition 1 through n, each containing at least two interval elements, and asks whether any has total reciprocal modulus below 0.98. August 2026 updates address other directions. This paraphrase records the inspected question, not an ownership claim.
sources.title: Gerry Myerson: finite residue covers and heft question

sources.excerpt: Myerson, Poon and Simpson introduced this finite covering-system setting and reported structural and computational results. The inspected primary search extract gives heft bounds in terms of interval length and number of classes; the full CORE PDF was unavailable to this audit.
sources.title: Incongruent restricted disjoint covering systems

sources.excerpt: The authors define incongruent restricted disjoint covering systems with at least two interval elements per congruence class and describe structural families and finite computations. The study preserves the original partition requirement.
sources.title: Incongruent Restricted Disjoint Covering Systems
